hypothesis.title: CT Radiomics Signature Predicts High‑Risk Neuroblastoma
hypothesis.intervention: Application of a radiomics‑derived imaging signature extracted from diagnostic CT scans
hypothesis.outcome: Accurate prediction of high‑risk disease status
hypothesis.clinical_context: Use of advanced CT radiomics analysis as a non‑invasive prognostic tool in neuroblastoma management

steps.name: Formulate Research Question & Objectives
steps.description: Define the primary hypothesis that a CT‑derived radiomics signature can accurately predict high‑risk neuroblastoma. Specify secondary objectives (e.g., comparison with current histopathologic risk stratification, assessment of inter‑observer reproducibility, evaluation of added clinical value).

steps.name: Comprehensive Literature Review
steps.description: Search PubMed, Embase, and Scopus for prior radiomics studies in neuroblastoma and related pediatric solid tumors. Summarize existing imaging protocols, feature extraction pipelines, and predictive modeling approaches to inform study design.

steps.name: Study Design Selection
steps.description: Choose a multicenter, retrospective‑prospective cohort design. The retrospective arm will provide initial model training using existing CT datasets; the prospective arm will validate the signature in real‑time clinical workflow.

steps.name: Develop Detailed Protocol
steps.description: Write a protocol covering inclusion/exclusion criteria, sample size calculation, CT acquisition parameters, radiomics pipeline, reference standard for high‑risk status (International Neuroblastoma Risk Group criteria), statistical analysis plan, and data management procedures.

steps.name: Ethics & Regulatory Approvals
steps.description: Submit the protocol to Institutional Review Boards (IRBs) at each participating site. Obtain parental consent/child assent for prospective enrollment and data use agreements for retrospective data sharing.

steps.name: Site Selection & Training
steps.description: Identify 4‑6 pediatric oncology centers with standardized diagnostic CT scanners. Conduct webinars and hands‑on workshops to train radiologists, technologists, and data scientists on uniform image acquisition, de‑identification, and radiomics feature extraction.

steps.name: Define Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria
steps.description: Inclusion: patients ≤ 18 years with histologically confirmed neuroblastoma and a diagnostic contrast‑enhanced CT performed < 30 days before treatment. Exclusion: prior chemotherapy/radiation before baseline CT, poor‑quality CT (motion artifacts), incomplete clinical data.

steps.name: Sample Size Determination
steps.description: Estimate based on expected AUC ≥ 0.80 for the radiomics model, prevalence of high‑risk disease (~40 %). Using an alpha of 0.05 and power = 0.90, calculate a required cohort of ≈250 patients (≈150 for training, 100 for validation).

steps.name: Retrospective Data Collection
steps.description: Gather de‑identified DICOM CT scans, pathology reports, and clinical variables (age, stage, MYCN status, serum markers). Store in a secure, centralized repository with a unique study ID for each patient.

steps.name: Standardize CT Acquisition & Pre‑processing
steps.description: Harmonize voxel spacing (e.g., resample to 1 mm³), apply intensity normalization, and segment primary tumor volume using semi‑automated software supervised by two pediatric radiologists. Record inter‑observer Dice coefficient.

steps.name: Radiomics Feature Extraction
steps.description: Use an open‑source toolbox (e.g., PyRadiomics) to extract first‑order statistics, shape descriptors, texture matrices (GLCM, GLRLM, GLSZM, NGTDM), and wavelet‑filtered features. Apply feature reproducibility filters (ICC ≥ 0.80).

steps.name: Feature Selection & Model Development
steps.description: Split retrospective cohort into training (70 %) and internal test (30 %) sets. Perform dimensionality reduction using variance thresholding, correlation analysis (remove r > 0.9), and regularized methods (LASSO). Build predictive models (logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting) and select the best based on cross‑validated AUC.

steps.name: Model Calibration & Decision Curve Analysis
steps.description: Assess calibration with Hosmer‑Lemeshow test and calibration plots. Conduct decision curve analysis to quantify net clinical benefit across risk thresholds.

steps.name: Prospective Validation
steps.description: Enroll new patients meeting inclusion criteria across sites. Apply the finalized radiomics signature in a blinded fashion to their baseline CTs. Compare model predictions with the reference standard high‑risk classification determined after complete diagnostic work‑up.

steps.name: Statistical Evaluation of Predictive Performance
steps.description: Compute sensitivity, specificity, positive/negative predictive values, accuracy, and AUC for the prospective cohort. Use DeLong’s test to compare radiomics AUC against traditional clinical risk models. Perform subgroup analyses (age groups, tumor site).

steps.name: Assess Added Value Over Standard Risk Factors
steps.description: Create multivariable logistic regression models incorporating clinical variables (age, stage, MYCN, ferritin, LDH) with and without the radiomics signature. Evaluate improvement via net reclassification index (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI).

steps.name: Health‑Economic Impact Modelling
steps.description: Model potential cost savings from earlier identification of high‑risk patients (e.g., reduced need for invasive biopsies, optimized chemotherapy intensity). Use a decision‑analytic framework to estimate incremental cost‑effectiveness ratios.

steps.name: Data Quality Auditing & Monitoring
steps.description: Implement periodic data audits to verify completeness, correct labeling of risk status, and adherence to imaging protocols. Resolve discrepancies through centralized query management.

steps.name: Manuscript Preparation & Dissemination
steps.description: Prepare a STROBE‑compliant manuscript describing methods, results, and implications. Submit to a high‑impact oncology or radiology journal. Present findings at pediatric oncology conferences and share the radiomics pipeline (code and configuration) on an open‑source repository.

steps.name: Regulatory & Clinical Implementation Planning
steps.description: Engage with health authorities to discuss qualification of the radiomics signature as a diagnostic decision support tool. Develop clinical workflow integration guidelines (e.g., PACS plug‑in) and educational material for clinicians.
